findings.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor assigns `options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` to the field declared as `private options: InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null;` (unchanged in the diff), and the two types are not mutually assignable, so the file fails typecheck. TypeScript cannot assign `{scope: "user" | "org" | "team"; userId: number; orgId: number; teamId?: number}` to the z.infer discriminated union: `scope` is a union of literals that is assignable to none of the members' literal `scope` types, and `teamId?: number` (optional) is not assignable to the team member's required `teamId: number`. The PR does not compile as written; the field declaration must also be changed (or the old type kept) for the build to pass.

[ADVISORY] The PR deletes the only query-execution entry point (`findMany`) and changes `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` from returning `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` to `Prisma.Sql`, yet the diff updates no consumer of this service outside its own test file. Any call site still calling `service.findMany(...)` or embedding the returned conditions into `prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany({ where })` (a Prisma.Sql is not a valid WhereInput) fails typecheck and breaks the build; the prerequisite migration of consumers is simply absent from this diff, so either those callers do not exist (findMany was dead code and should have been flagged as such) or the PR is incomplete.

[ADVISORY] The new hand-written `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` duplicates the shape already encoded in the exported zod `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema` (which remains in the file and still backs `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`), creating two parallel hand-maintained sources of truth for the same options shape. The next change to the options surface (e.g. a new scope or a new required field) must be made in both the zod schema and the hand-written type; miss one and the constructor silently accepts shapes the schema rejects or vice versa. The hand-written type also drops the schema's per-scope guarantees (e.g. `teamId` required only for the team scope), so the zod schema no longer describes what the constructor actually accepts.

[ADVISORY] The entire "Caching" describe block (both the authorization-conditions and filter-conditions cache tests) is deleted even though the caching mechanism (`cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` short-circuit in `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions`) is retained in the service. The retained per-instance memoization now has zero test coverage: a regression that makes the getters rebuild conditions on every call (extra DB round trips via `isOrgOwnerOrAdmin`, TeamRepository, MembershipRepository on every invocation) or, worse, return a stale half-initialized `Sql` from the cache, would pass CI unnoticed.

[ADVISORY] The service's only query-execution method `findMany` is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, but the diff contains no migration for any existing caller of `service.findMany`, silently dropping the acceptance criterion that consumers of InsightsBookingService keep working. Every existing caller that invoked findMany (as the deleted test did) now fails to compile or must hand-write raw SQL with its own hardcoded `"BookingTimeStatusDenormalized"` table name; if this PR merges without those call-site migrations, insights endpoints break, and if callers are updated elsewhere the pagination/select abstraction is duplicated at each site.

[ADVISORY] The constructor signature was widened from the zod-validated discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the flat `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, which drops the compile-time guarantee that `scope: "team"` carries a `teamId` (teamId is now optional for every scope). A caller can now construct `{scope: "team", userId, orgId}` with no teamId, which the discriminated union previously rejected at compile time; buildTeamAuthorizationCondition then interpolates `options.teamId` (undefined) into `Prisma.sql` (`"teamId" = ${options.teamId}`) and passes it to findByIdAndParentId, producing a runtime failure or silently wrong authorization scoping instead of a construction-time error.

[ADVISORY] The entire `Caching` describe block ("should cache authorization conditions" / "should cache filter conditions") is deleted while the caching fields `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` and the memoization logic in getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions remain in insightsBooking.ts, leaving the caching behavior with zero verification. A future regression that breaks memoization (e.g., reassigning the cache field, or returning a fresh Sql per call) will pass CI silently; the second-call behavior of these now-public methods is untested even though getBaseConditions depends on it.

[ADVISORY] All authorization and filter predicates are now hand-written raw SQL with hardcoded quoted column names ("eventTypeId", "eventParentId", "userId", "teamId", "isTeamBooking"), replacing typed `BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` objects that the Prisma schema previously kept in sync. A column rename on BookingTimeStatusDenormalized in the Prisma schema now passes typecheck everywhere in the codebase and only surfaces at runtime as a Postgres "column does not exist" error on insights endpoints; the previous where-input typing turned this into a compile error.

[ADVISORY] The `else if (filterConditions)` and `else` branches in getBaseConditions are dead code: getAuthorizationConditions always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql (buildAuthorizationConditions returns NOTHING_CONDITION on every fallback path), so the first two branches cover all reachable states. Readers and future maintainers must reason about an unreachable 'no authorization conditions' state that cannot occur; deleting the two dead branches removes two code paths with no behavior change.

[ADVISORY] buildOrgAuthorizationCondition unconditionally emits `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` even when `teamIds` is empty (an org with no child teams, reachable when findAllByParentId returns []), and no test in this diff covers the empty-array case — every test passes a non-empty array. The old Prisma `in: []` path was a guaranteed engine-level no-match; the new empty-array parameter binding to `= ANY(...)` on this reachable path (org-scoped insights for an org without sub-teams) is completely unverified and is a known parameter-typing failure mode in Postgres raw queries, risking a 500 or silently wrong scoping for those tenants.

[ADVISORY] getBaseConditions() is a new public API whose returned SQL references unqualified column names ("userId", "teamId", "isTeamBooking"), making the contract only safe when embedded in a query against exactly one table with no alias/join. The next consumer who embeds baseConditions into a query that joins any table also containing a userId or teamId column gets a Postgres "column reference is ambiguous" error at runtime, with nothing in the method name or type signature warning them.

[BUG] getBaseConditions() and buildOrgAuthorizationCondition() return Prisma.Sql fragments whose top-level OR is unparenthesized, so any caller composing `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <extra filter>` gets `A OR B AND extra`, which Postgres evaluates as `A OR (B AND extra)`. Authorization bypass by precedence: rows matching the first OR branch (e.g., all team bookings of the org) are returned even when they fail the caller's additional filter, and rows in the second branch silently lose the extra filter — the old Prisma WhereInput composition guaranteed correct nesting, the raw-SQL contract does not, and nothing in getBaseConditions' signature or the diff documents that the fragment is only safe as a complete WHERE clause.

[BUG] The PR titled 'convert to Prisma.sql raw queries' also removes the public findMany() method, swaps the constructor's option type from the zod-inferred discriminated union to a new hand-written InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions, and refactors isOrgOwnerOrAdmin — API-surface work not traceable to the stated conversion intent, with no consumer migration anywhere in the diff. Any call site that instantiated InsightsBookingService with the zod-shaped options or called service.findMany() fails to compile (or, if untyped, now receives a Prisma.Sql where a WhereInput object is expected and Prisma throws at runtime); the diff updates only the service and its own test, so either findMany was dead code (untraceable work) or the migration of consumers is missing from this PR.

[BUG] InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes teamId optional for every scope, replacing the discriminated union's per-scope guarantees with a flat type, while buildTeamAuthorizationCondition still interpolates options.teamId directly into SQL. An options object `{scope: "team", userId, orgId}` without teamId now type-checks at the constructor; at query time `Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ${undefined})" binds undefined and Prisma throws, turning a compile-time contract violation into a 500. The exported zod schema remains as a second, now-divorced source of truth for the same shape, so future schema changes will drift from this hand-maintained type.

[ADVISORY] The entire 'Caching' describe block is deleted even though the caching behavior itself is retained and its implementation lines are modified in this diff (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions retyped to Prisma.Sql). The cache-once invariant of getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions is now enforced by zero tests; a regression that rebuilds conditions on every call (re-running the TeamRepository/MembershipRepository queries per request) or, worse, returns a stale first-call result would land undetected — the diff touches the cached fields but removes the only tests guarding them.

[ADVISORY] Two of the four branches in getBaseConditions() are dead code: buildAuthorizationConditions is typed Promise<Prisma.Sql> (never null), so `authConditions` is always truthy and the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches are unreachable. Future maintainers reading the branch structure conclude filter-only or condition-less services are supported states and preserve the branching through later changes; deleting the two unreachable branches (and the implicit contract question they raise) removes two places-to-update on every edit to this method.

[BUG] The public method findMany() is deleted and replaced by getBaseConditions() returning a raw Prisma.Sql fragment, but the diff contains no updates to any caller of findMany, so every existing consumer of InsightsBookingService breaks. At best, in-repo callers fail TypeScript compilation at deploy; at worst (JS callers or partial rollouts) they hit 'service.findMany is not a function' at runtime and insights endpoints 500. Even for callers that are migrated, this is an unversioned breaking contract change: consumers previously composed typed Prisma where-inputs into arbitrary findManyArgs and now must hand-write $queryRaw against a specific physical table.

[ADVISORY] The new public API shape exports raw SQL fragments built from unqualified, hard-coded physical column names ("userId", "teamId", "isTeamBooking", "eventTypeId", "eventParentId") with Postgres-only syntax (= ANY(...), bare true), binding every consumer to one table, one dialect, and one naming scheme. Any consumer who composes these fragments into a query that joins another table with a same-named column (Booking itself has userId and teamId) gets a Postgres 'column reference is ambiguous' error or silently scopes to the wrong table — the new integration test only passes because it queries the single table with no join. A Prisma schema column rename that TypeScript previously caught in the typed where-input now surfaces as a runtime SQL error. The service boundary changed from a typed, composable, dialect-agnostic contract to a leaked internal representation.

[ADVISORY] InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions hand-duplicates the shape already defined by insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema (z.infer), and the two copies already disagree in this diff: teamId is optional in the new manual type for all scopes but required in the 'team' variant of the zod union, while the constructor still stores into `this.options: InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null`. An invalid options object (e.g. {scope:'team'} without teamId) that previously failed type-checking now compiles; if the constructor still safeParses into the zod type, it degrades to options=null → NOTHING_CONDITION, so the caller gets a silently empty dashboard instead of a compile-time or explicit error. The next change to the options shape must be made in two places or the copies drift further.

[BUG] buildOrgAuthorizationCondition passes teamIds unguarded into = ANY(${teamIds}), so an org with zero child teams binds an empty JS array as the SQL parameter, a path the old typed layer handled via Prisma's `in: []` rendering. If the Prisma query engine/Postgres cannot infer an element type for the empty array parameter, every insights request from an org owner whose org has no sub-teams fails with a parameter-type/SQL error instead of returning data; the userIds arrays got an explicit length guard in this diff but teamIds did not, showing the empty-collection case was considered only for one of the two arrays.

[ADVISORY] The Caching test block is deleted from this diff, but the caching mechanism it covered (cachedAuthConditions / cachedFilterConditions memoization keyed on `=== undefined`) is retained unchanged in insightsBooking.ts. The per-instance memoization of authorization/filter conditions is now completely untested; a regression that re-issues the membership/team lookups on every getBaseConditions call (e.g. someone 'simplifying' the undefined checks) or one that wrongly caches a null would ship green.

[ADVISORY] Three hand-rolled copies of the same reduce-with-index-0 fragment joiner (AND in buildFilterConditions, OR in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, OR in buildTeamAuthorizationCondition) duplicate the parenthesization/join logic instead of one shared and()/or() helper. The next condition added to any of the three builders risks copying the reduce with the wrong operator or forgetting the paren-wrapping of the accumulator — a precedence bug that only manifests when the fragment is combined with others in getBaseConditions; a single helper collapses all three sites and makes the operator explicit at each call site.

[BUG] The diff deletes the public findMany() method entirely and replaces it with getBaseConditions(), silently changing the PR objective from 'convert the service to Prisma.sql raw queries' to 'remove the service's data-access API and require every consumer to hand-write raw $queryRaw calls', with no call-site migration shown anywhere in this diff. Every existing caller of InsightsBookingService.findMany() outside these two files breaks at compile time (or, if updated ad hoc, each caller now manually interpolates getBaseConditions() into its own SQL). The old design made authorization non-bypassable: auth conditions were merged inside findMany so callers could not query without them. After this change, authorization enforcement is opt-in per caller — any new or modified consumer that forgets to embed getBaseConditions() returns unauthorized cross-team booking data. This is an objective change (API removal + security-encapsulation removal) that the PR title does not declare and no explicit human acceptance is recorded for.

[ADVISORY] The entire 'Caching' describe block is deleted while the caching behavior it verified (cachedAuthConditions / cachedFilterConditions fields and the undefined-sentinel memoization in getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions) is retained unchanged in insightsBooking.ts lines 86-99. The only tests proving that repeated calls reuse cached conditions (and that a null filter condition is cached as null rather than recomputed) are gone without replacement — the tests were dropped rather than converted, presumably because Prisma.Sql cache-value comparison was awkward to assert. Anyone refactoring the memoization (e.g., flipping the undefined sentinel or removing the cache during another raw-SQL iteration) ships a silent N+1-style regression of repeat DB condition-building with zero test signal; the accepted caching behavior survives in code only by accident.

[ADVISORY] InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions is a second, hand-maintained copy of the options shape already defined by insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema (the zod discriminated union two lines above), and the class field this.options is still typed as the zod-inferred union while being assigned from the flat public type — two sources of truth for the same contract. The next change to options (adding a scope, renaming a field, making teamId required for team scope) must be applied in both the zod schema and this parallel type; when they drift, the constructor accepts at the type boundary an object the rest of the class assumes satisfies the discriminated union — e.g., a caller passing {scope: 'team', userId, orgId} without teamId is legal against the flat type but reaches Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ${options.teamId})` with undefined, turning a former compile-time rejection into a runtime failure at query execution.

[ADVISORY] Two of the four branches in getBaseConditions are dead: getAuthorizationConditions() is declared and implemented as non-nullable (it returns NOTHING_CONDITION, never null), so 'authConditions &&' is always true and both the filter-only branch and the final NOTHING_CONDITION else branch are unreachable. Readers and future editors reasonably infer that a no-filters/no-auth state is a reachable runtime case and preserve the branches; the deletion test applies — dropping the two dead branches (and the non-null narrowing on a non-nullable value) removes two places-to-reason-about with zero behavior change. The next person changing condition composition has to work out from scratch that these paths cannot fire.

[ADVISORY] The converted tests now assert exact internal SQL text (parenthesization, ANY(...) spelling, column quoting) via toEqual on Prisma.Sql instead of asserting the semantic conditions the previous expectations expressed, coupling the suite to the implementation's string formatting. A purely cosmetic refactor of buildAuthorizationConditions/buildFilterConditions (reordering the AND operands, adding or removing redundant parentheses, switching = ANY(...) to IN (...)) changes zero runtime behavior but breaks four tests in this file, training future contributors to mechanically update expected SQL strings rather than verify authorization semantics — the test objective silently shifted from 'these are the authorized rows' to 'this is the exact SQL'.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes the findMany() method, which was the structural chokepoint guaranteeing that every query on BookingTimeStatusDenormalized carried the authorization conditions, and replaces it with a public getBaseConditions() that hands callers a raw Prisma.Sql fragment they must remember to embed in their own $queryRaw calls. Any caller (the diff's own test shows the new intended pattern: prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" WHERE ${baseConditions}`) that composes a raw query and forgets to interpolate getBaseConditions(), or applies it to the wrong table/alias, silently returns cross-tenant booking data with no compile-time or runtime error — the previous design made an unscoped query impossible to write through the service, the new one makes it the default mistake.

[ADVISORY] The authorization fragments use unqualified quoted column names ("teamId", "userId", "isTeamBooking") that are now exported as reusable Prisma.Sql values, so they only resolve correctly when the caller's query has BookingTimeStatusDenormalized as the sole table in scope. A caller embedding getBaseConditions() into a query that joins any other table containing userId or teamId gets either a 'column reference is ambiguous' runtime error (500 on the insights endpoint) or, in a join where the unqualified name binds to the other table, the authorization predicate evaluated against the wrong table's rows — the old typed Prisma where-input was table-scoped by construction and could not be mis-bound.

[ADVISORY] The entire 'Caching' describe block (both 'should cache authorization conditions' and 'should cache filter conditions' tests) is deleted in this diff while the caching behavior it covered is retained unchanged in insightsBooking.ts (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions fields and the `if (this.cachedAuthConditions === undefined)` lazy-build branches). The lazy-cache lifecycle is now the only service behavior with zero test coverage: a regression in the cache check (e.g., a future change making the `=== undefined` comparison miss a cached null, or rebuilding the SQL on every call so multi-call request paths issue repeated DB round-trips via TeamRepository/MembershipRepository) would pass this suite. Anyone later modifying getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions has no test that detects a broken second-call path, and the deletion is silent — no replacement test covers the retained `=== undefined` caching branches.

[ADVISORY] The org-scope authorization test (and likewise the team-scope, NOTHING, and filter-condition tests at lines ~273, ~295, ~384, ~407, ~429) asserts the produced Prisma.Sql by exact string equality against a hand-typed copy of the implementation's template, and never executes that SQL against the database — the mirror test verifies the code against itself, not against query semantics. The only assertion in the diff that actually runs generated SQL is the final getBaseConditions test, which exercises solely the user-scope path (`("userId" = ${...}) AND ("teamId" IS NULL)`). If any of the never-executed templates is invalid at the driver/Postgres level — e.g., `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` passing a raw JS array as a single bind parameter, or `"isTeamBooking" = true` being sent as a text param — every string-equality test still passes because the test literal was copied from the same broken source. The suite reports green on the org/team authorization paths while those queries have never been proven executable; the first real insights dashboard request for an org/team-scoped user is where the failure surfaces.

[ADVISORY] getBaseConditions is a new four-branch combination function (both conditions, auth-only, filter-only, NOTHING fallback) but the only test in the diff that calls it is 'should combine authorization and filter conditions', which exercises exclusively the both-conditions branch. Checked the sole test file in the diff (packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts): every getFilterConditions test calls the method directly and every auth test calls getAuthorizationConditions directly, so the auth-only, filter-only, and `return NOTHING_CONDITION` fallback branches of getBaseConditions are never executed. A regression in the branch order (e.g., the else returning authConditions instead of NOTHING_CONDITION when options is null, which would leak all bookings to an unscoped caller instead of returning nothing) is invisible to this suite despite the branch being the security-relevant fallback.

[ADVISORY] The new `if (userIdsFromOrg.length > 0)` guard branch in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (the empty-membership path that emits only the team-booking SQL) has no test that triggers it. Checked the diff's only test file: every org-scope test seeds an org with teams and members (testData.org, team2, team3, user2, user3), so the guard's false path is never executed. This path is exactly where a driver-level failure mode lives — `("userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds}))` is skipped, but `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` with `teamIds = []` (org with no sub-teams) still executes; whether Prisma/Postgres accepts an empty-array bind for `= ANY($1)` is unverified, and the first org with zero sub-teams would be where a 'could not determine data type' or binding error appears, in production rather than in CI.

[ADVISORY] The new `if (userIdsFromTeam.length > 0)` guard branch in buildTeamAuthorizationCondition (the path that omits the user-booking OR arm when the team has no members) has no test that triggers it. Checked the diff's only test file (insightsBooking.integration-test.ts): the team-scope test seeds members into the team, so the empty-membership arm is never exercised. Note this guard also silently changed behavior versus the old code (which always emitted a `userId: { in: [...] }` OR arm even for empty arrays): the equivalence 'empty IN-list is falsy ≡ omitting the arm' is an untested semantic assumption, and if the team-scope SQL with a single-member ANY() list or the omitted-arm path is wrong, no test in this diff can detect it.

[ADVISORY] The org-scope and team-scope authorization conditions now rely on Prisma raw-parameter binding of JS arrays via `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` / `("userId" = ANY(${userIds}))`, and no test in this diff ever executes those conditions against the database — every org/team assertion is a structural `toEqual` on the Prisma.Sql object, and the only `$queryRaw` execution (the getBaseConditions test) exercises the user scope, which contains no ANY() array binding. If Prisma's serialization of a JS array parameter for `= ANY($1)` misbehaves (e.g., type inference or empty-array handling), every org- and team-scope insights dashboard query throws at runtime and 500s for admins, and no test in this diff would catch it before production.

[ADVISORY] The raw SQL strings hardcode the table name "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" and column identifiers "teamId", "isTeamBooking", "userId", "eventTypeId", "eventParentId" as string literals, replacing Prisma's compile-time schema verification with identifiers that are only checked when the query executes. A future Prisma schema rename or @@map change that the old typed where-inputs would have caught at build time now ships silently and surfaces as a runtime database error (500) on every insights request that reaches the affected condition.

[ADVISORY] The new InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type is hand-maintained parallel to insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema and declares `teamId?: number` optional, whereas the zod discriminated union requires teamId for scope "team" (buildTeamAuthorizationCondition reads options.teamId as a required field), so a caller can now pass options that are TypeScript-valid but fail zod validation. A call site constructing the service with scope "team" and no teamId — previously a compile error under the zod-inferred type — now compiles and throws ZodError at construction time, turning what was a build-time failure into a runtime 500 on the request path.

goldens.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor assigns `options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` to the field declared as `private options: InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null;` (unchanged in the diff), and the two types are not mutually assignable, so the file fails typecheck. TypeScript cannot assign `{scope: "user" | "org" | "team"; userId: number; orgId: number; teamId?: number}` to the z.infer discriminated union: `scope` is a union of literals that is assignable to none of the members' literal `scope` types, and `teamId?: number` (optional) is not assignable to the team member's required `teamId: number`. The PR does not compile as written; the field declaration must also be changed (or the old type kept) for the build to pass.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the constructor does not assign the `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` value directly to `this.options`. It assigns `this.options = insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.parse(options);`, and `parse(...)` returns the schema’s inferred type (`InsightsBookingServiceOptions`), which matches the field type `InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null`. Therefore the claimed TypeScript assignability/typecheck failure is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR deletes the only query-execution entry point (`findMany`) and changes `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` from returning `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` to `Prisma.Sql`, yet the diff updates no consumer of this service outside its own test file. Any call site still calling `service.findMany(...)` or embedding the returned conditions into `prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany({ where })` (a Prisma.Sql is not a valid WhereInput) fails typecheck and breaks the build; the prerequisite migration of consumers is simply absent from this diff, so either those callers do not exist (findMany was dead code and should have been flagged as such) or the PR is incomplete.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes `findMany` from `InsightsBookingService` and changes `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` to return `Prisma.Sql` instead of `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` (and updates only the integration test to use `$queryRaw` + `getBaseConditions`). This is a breaking API change for any external callers of `service.findMany(...)` or callers expecting WhereInput-shaped conditions, but the diff provides no evidence of migrating any consumers beyond this test file. Whether such consumers exist cannot be verified from the diff alone, so it’s a real, specific risk/incompleteness concern rather than a provable build break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new hand-written `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` duplicates the shape already encoded in the exported zod `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema` (which remains in the file and still backs `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`), creating two parallel hand-maintained sources of truth for the same options shape. The next change to the options surface (e.g. a new scope or a new required field) must be made in both the zod schema and the hand-written type; miss one and the constructor silently accepts shapes the schema rejects or vice versa. The hand-written type also drops the schema's per-scope guarantees (e.g. `teamId` required only for the team scope), so the zod schema no longer describes what the constructor actually accepts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new hand-written `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` and changes the constructor to accept it (`options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`) while the file still defines and exports the zod-backed `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema` / `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`. This creates parallel definitions of the options surface. The new public type is less specific (e.g., `teamId?: number` regardless of `scope`), while downstream methods still assume per-scope fields (e.g., `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` uses `options.teamId`), so the constructor’s accepted shape is no longer aligned with the discriminated union schema/type. This is a concrete maintainability/typing-contract regression grounded in the diff, even if it may not immediately manifest as a runtime crash.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire "Caching" describe block (both the authorization-conditions and filter-conditions cache tests) is deleted even though the caching mechanism (`cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` short-circuit in `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions`) is retained in the service. The retained per-instance memoization now has zero test coverage: a regression that makes the getters rebuild conditions on every call (extra DB round trips via `isOrgOwnerOrAdmin`, TeamRepository, MembershipRepository on every invocation) or, worse, return a stale half-initialized `Sql` from the cache, would pass CI unnoticed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getBaseConditions() and buildOrgAuthorizationCondition() return Prisma.Sql fragments whose top-level OR is unparenthesized, so any caller composing `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <extra filter>` gets `A OR B AND extra`, which Postgres evaluates as `A OR (B AND extra)`. Authorization bypass by precedence: rows matching the first OR branch (e.g., all team bookings of the org) are returned even when they fail the caller's additional filter, and rows in the second branch silently lose the extra filter — the old Prisma WhereInput composition guaranteed correct nesting, the raw-SQL contract does not, and nothing in getBaseConditions' signature or the diff documents that the fragment is only safe as a complete WHERE clause.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition()` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition()` build OR-chains via `conditions.reduce(... That means a caller doing `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <extra>` can indeed generate `A OR B AND extra` instead of `(A OR B) AND extra`, changing semantics and potentially bypassing intended filtering/authorization. This risk is introduced by switching from Prisma `WhereInput` composition to raw SQL fragments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff deletes the findMany() method, which was the structural chokepoint guaranteeing that every query on BookingTimeStatusDenormalized carried the authorization conditions, and replaces it with a public getBaseConditions() that hands callers a raw Prisma.Sql fragment they must remember to embed in their own $queryRaw calls. Any caller (the diff's own test shows the new intended pattern: prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" WHERE ${baseConditions}`) that composes a raw query and forgets to interpolate getBaseConditions(), or applies it to the wrong table/alias, silently returns cross-tenant booking data with no compile-time or runtime error — the previous design made an unscoped query impossible to write through the service, the new one makes it the default mistake.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `findMany()` wrapper that previously always injected `authConditions`/`filterConditions` into the Prisma `where` clause, and replaces it with a public `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>` that returns a SQL fragment (see `InsightsBookingService.getBaseConditions`). The updated test demonstrates the intended new usage pattern: callers must manually embed the fragment into `$queryRaw` (`WHERE ${baseConditions}`). This change does create an easy-to-misuse API where future callers could omit or misapply the condition and bypass scoping, but the diff itself does not show an actual callsite doing so, so it’s an architectural/safety concern rather than a verifiable defect introduced in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The authorization fragments use unqualified quoted column names ("teamId", "userId", "isTeamBooking") that are now exported as reusable Prisma.Sql values, so they only resolve correctly when the caller's query has BookingTimeStatusDenormalized as the sole table in scope. A caller embedding getBaseConditions() into a query that joins any other table containing userId or teamId gets either a 'column reference is ambiguous' runtime error (500 on the insights endpoint) or, in a join where the unqualified name binds to the other table, the authorization predicate evaluated against the wrong table's rows — the old typed Prisma where-input was table-scoped by construction and could not be mis-bound.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes conditions from model-scoped Prisma where-inputs to reusable `Prisma.Sql` fragments (e.g., `Prisma.sql`"userId" = ...`, `"teamId" = ...`, `"isTeamBooking" = ...`) returned by `getBaseConditions()` / `getAuthorizationConditions()` / `getFilterConditions()`. Those SQL snippets use unqualified column names throughout (no table name/alias), so if a caller embeds them into a raw query that includes joins with overlapping column names, they can become ambiguous or bind to the wrong table. The diff does not show an actual joined-query usage causing a runtime failure, so it's a concrete diff-grounded design/correctness risk rather than a proven bug in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire 'Caching' describe block (both 'should cache authorization conditions' and 'should cache filter conditions' tests) is deleted in this diff while the caching behavior it covered is retained unchanged in insightsBooking.ts (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions fields and the `if (this.cachedAuthConditions === undefined)` lazy-build branches). The lazy-cache lifecycle is now the only service behavior with zero test coverage: a regression in the cache check (e.g., a future change making the `=== undefined` comparison miss a cached null, or rebuilding the SQL on every call so multi-call request paths issue repeated DB round-trips via TeamRepository/MembershipRepository) would pass this suite. Anyone later modifying getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions has no test that detects a broken second-call path, and the deletion is silent — no replacement test covers the retained `=== undefined` caching branches.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the entire `describe("Caching")` block from `insightsBooking.integration-test.ts`, including tests that called `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` twice to assert the second call reuses cached results. In `insightsBooking.ts`, the lazy caching behavior is still present (`cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` fields and `if (this.cachedAuthConditions === undefined)` / `if (this.cachedFilterConditions === undefined)` guards). The remaining tests assert condition values but do not exercise the second-call cache path, so the caching branches are no longer covered by this suite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The org-scope authorization test (and likewise the team-scope, NOTHING, and filter-condition tests at lines ~273, ~295, ~384, ~407, ~429) asserts the produced Prisma.Sql by exact string equality against a hand-typed copy of the implementation's template, and never executes that SQL against the database — the mirror test verifies the code against itself, not against query semantics. The only assertion in the diff that actually runs generated SQL is the final getBaseConditions test, which exercises solely the user-scope path (`("userId" = ${...}) AND ("teamId" IS NULL)`). If any of the never-executed templates is invalid at the driver/Postgres level — e.g., `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` passing a raw JS array as a single bind parameter, or `"isTeamBooking" = true` being sent as a text param — every string-equality test still passes because the test literal was copied from the same broken source. The suite reports green on the org/team authorization paths while those queries have never been proven executable; the first real insights dashboard request for an org/team-scoped user is where the failure surfaces.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes multiple tests to `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` (e.g., user/org/team auth and filter tests) which compares the returned `Prisma.Sql` object to a hand-written `Prisma.sql` template rather than executing it. Only the new `getBaseConditions` test actually runs SQL via `$queryRaw` (`WHERE ${baseConditions}`), and it exercises the user-scope path; org/team-scope SQL fragments are never executed in the tests shown. This is a concrete test-quality gap introduced by the diff (mirror testing), but not a directly verifiable production defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getBaseConditions is a new four-branch combination function (both conditions, auth-only, filter-only, NOTHING fallback) but the only test in the diff that calls it is 'should combine authorization and filter conditions', which exercises exclusively the both-conditions branch. Checked the sole test file in the diff (packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts): every getFilterConditions test calls the method directly and every auth test calls getAuthorizationConditions directly, so the auth-only, filter-only, and `return NOTHING_CONDITION` fallback branches of getBaseConditions are never executed. A regression in the branch order (e.g., the else returning authConditions instead of NOTHING_CONDITION when options is null, which would leak all bookings to an unscoped caller instead of returning nothing) is invisible to this suite despite the branch being the security-relevant fallback.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `getBaseConditions()` with four explicit branches in `packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts` (both auth+filter -> `AND`, auth-only, filter-only, else -> `NOTHING_CONDITION`). In the updated integration test file, only the renamed `describe("getBaseConditions")` test invokes `getBaseConditions()` and it sets both `options` and `filters`, so it exercises only the `if (authConditions && filterConditions)` branch. All other tests still call `getAuthorizationConditions()` or `getFilterConditions()` directly, so the auth-only, filter-only, and fallback branches of `getBaseConditions()` are indeed unexecuted by this suite. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-coverage concern for newly added branching logic rather than a demonstrated functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new `if (userIdsFromOrg.length > 0)` guard branch in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (the empty-membership path that emits only the team-booking SQL) has no test that triggers it. Checked the diff's only test file: every org-scope test seeds an org with teams and members (testData.org, team2, team3, user2, user3), so the guard's false path is never executed. This path is exactly where a driver-level failure mode lives — `("userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds}))` is skipped, but `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` with `teamIds = []` (org with no sub-teams) still executes; whether Prisma/Postgres accepts an empty-array bind for `= ANY($1)` is unverified, and the first org with zero sub-teams would be where a 'could not determine data type' or binding error appears, in production rather than in CI.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds a new guard in `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` that only appends the user-booking OR clause when `userIdsFromOrg.length > 0`, and always emits `Prisma.sql` with `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)` even if `teamIds` is empty. In the integration test updates, the org-scope authorization test shown constructs additional teams/users (`team2`, `team3`, `user2`, `user3`) so `userIdsFromOrg.length > 0` is exercised, but there is no test case in this diff that clearly drives the `userIdsFromOrg.length === 0` path (or the `teamIds === []` path). The claimed runtime failure with `ANY([])` is plausible but not provable from the diff alone, so this is best classified as a missing edge-case test / risk introduced by the change rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new `if (userIdsFromTeam.length > 0)` guard branch in buildTeamAuthorizationCondition (the path that omits the user-booking OR arm when the team has no members) has no test that triggers it. Checked the diff's only test file (insightsBooking.integration-test.ts): the team-scope test seeds members into the team, so the empty-membership arm is never exercised. Note this guard also silently changed behavior versus the old code (which always emitted a `userId: { in: [...] }` OR arm even for empty arrays): the equivalence 'empty IN-list is falsy ≡ omitting the arm' is an untested semantic assumption, and if the team-scope SQL with a single-member ANY() list or the omitted-arm path is wrong, no test in this diff can detect it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new guard in `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` that only appends the user-booking OR arm when `userIdsFromTeam.length > 0` (previously it always emitted a `userId in [...]` arm even if empty). In the updated integration tests, the team-scope expectation explicitly includes a `"userId" = ANY(${[testData.user.id]})` clause, meaning the test data path includes at least one team member, so the empty-membership branch (omitted OR arm) is not exercised. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing test/untested semantic change, not a proven defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The org-scope and team-scope authorization conditions now rely on Prisma raw-parameter binding of JS arrays via `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` / `("userId" = ANY(${userIds}))`, and no test in this diff ever executes those conditions against the database — every org/team assertion is a structural `toEqual` on the Prisma.Sql object, and the only `$queryRaw` execution (the getBaseConditions test) exercises the user scope, which contains no ANY() array binding. If Prisma's serialization of a JS array parameter for `= ANY($1)` misbehaves (e.g., type inference or empty-array handling), every org- and team-scope insights dashboard query throws at runtime and 500s for admins, and no test in this diff would catch it before production.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes org/team authorization builders to emit raw SQL using `= ANY(${...})` with JS arrays (e.g., `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition`). In the integration tests, org/team cases now only do `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...ANY(${[...]})...`)` structural assertions and never execute those `Prisma.Sql` fragments against the database. The only `$queryRaw` execution added is in the `getBaseConditions` test and uses `scope: "user"`, which does not exercise any `ANY(array)` binding. So if Prisma’s parameterization/type inference for arrays or empty-array handling causes runtime SQL errors, this diff’s tests would not catch it; this is a concrete missing runtime-coverage issue introduced by the switch to raw SQL, not a proven defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The raw SQL strings hardcode the table name "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" and column identifiers "teamId", "isTeamBooking", "userId", "eventTypeId", "eventParentId" as string literals, replacing Prisma's compile-time schema verification with identifiers that are only checked when the query executes. A future Prisma schema rename or @@map change that the old typed where-inputs would have caught at build time now ships silently and surfaces as a runtime database error (500) on every insights request that reaches the affected condition.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces Prisma typed where-input objects with raw SQL fragments using string-literal identifiers (e.g., `Prisma.sql\`("userId" = ... )\`` and `"teamId"`, `"isTeamBooking"`, `"eventTypeId"`, `"eventParentId"` throughout `insightsBooking.ts`). The integration test also now uses `$queryRaw` with a hardcoded table name `"BookingTimeStatusDenormalized"`. This change does remove Prisma’s compile-time/schema-driven verification of field/table names, making future renames/@@map changes more likely to surface only at runtime. That’s a concrete maintainability/robustness concern introduced by this diff, but not a current, directly verifiable runtime bug in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type is hand-maintained parallel to insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema and declares `teamId?: number` optional, whereas the zod discriminated union requires teamId for scope "team" (buildTeamAuthorizationCondition reads options.teamId as a required field), so a caller can now pass options that are TypeScript-valid but fail zod validation. A call site constructing the service with scope "team" and no teamId — previously a compile error under the zod-inferred type — now compiles and throws ZodError at construction time, turning what was a build-time failure into a runtime 500 on the request path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` with `teamId?: number` optional, and the constructor now accepts this type (`options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`) but still immediately does `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.parse(options)`. The zod schema (a discriminated union on `scope`) can require `teamId` when `scope` is "team", while the TS type no longer enforces that at compile time. This creates a real mismatch where TypeScript-valid inputs can now throw at runtime during construction; the diff doesn’t show an actual call site passing invalid options, so it’s not a proven broken behavior in this PR, but it is a concrete API/type-safety issue introduced here.
